name: Parsimony
overview: The Scriptures reveal a tension surrounding parsimony, especially evident in the disciples' reaction to the costly ointment poured on Jesus, which they deemed wasteful and argued could have been sold to aid the poor (Matthew 26:8-9). This incident highlights a misunderstanding of the value of honoring Christ above material concerns. Additionally, the book of Haggai illustrates the consequences of neglecting God's house and pursuing self-interest, resulting in diminished blessings and divine discipline, including drought and loss (Haggai 1:9-11). Together, these passages teach that parsimony, when rooted in selfishness or misplaced priorities, leads to spiritual and material loss, whereas true devotion to Christ transcends mere economy.
